trial_metrics: Observed average QPS during trial: 7 req/s (low sample traffic)
Average concurrency observed in trial: 6 simultaneous streams
Typical request token profile (trial): prompt ~140 tokens, completion ~420 tokens
Token mix observed: ~25% prompt tokens / 75% completion tokens (long-form answers & summaries)
95th percentile latency (hosted API in trial): ~420ms for most requests; heavy prompts up to ~900ms
Error rate: <0.2% (mostly rate-limit during burst test)
production_forecast_assumptions: Target steady-state QPS for launch: 120 req/s (month 1)
Peak concurrency planning: up to 250 concurrent streams for 15-30 minute bursts
Expected token mix in prod: prompt ~160 tokens, completion ~280 tokens (shorter replies on avg)
Monthly token volume estimate (prod month 1): ~1.1B tokens
SLO targets: median latency <200ms, 95th <450ms for chat flows
dedicated_capacity_requirements: Primary plan: reserved Dedicated pool in US-East with EU-populated model replicas for data residency
Model mix: default to 13B quantized for 70% of traffic; failover + special routes to 70B for complex summarization and code tasks
Batching strategy: use continuous batching + prefix caching for long sessions to reduce per-token cost
Autoscaling needs: baseline reserved GPUs to handle steady 120 QPS, burst pool to cover peaks to 350 QPS; request proposal for commit tiers (100/300/500 QPS)
KMS integration: require customer-managed keys for EU data at rest
Observability: token-level cost dashboards, per-route latency breakdown, trace hooks into their APM
requirements_summary: Workloads: in-app assistant (real-time chat) + semantic search embeddings + reranking for search results
Latency: strict median and tail latency SLAs for UI interactions
Throughput: plans for fast growth — sizing needs to be elastic but predictable
Security/compliance: SOC2 required, SSO/SAML, audit logging, EU data residency, KMS/HSM integration
Routing: multi-region routing (NA primary, EU for EU users) with automated fallback to NA if capacity constrained
Model policy: prefer open-weight models; Redwood verification of latency/cost tradeoffs is key
